title: From violin to the school band and a C melody saxophone
summary: Cobb is the lone violin in an 80-piece brass band, the instructor hands him a C melody saxophone with his mother's consent, and he learns it by transferring his piano and violin knowledge.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, now, let's get back to the violin.
I liked everything I did during those days because it was activities for me and it was very interesting. I took the 50 lessons; my mother financed it. And I got it and I got my violin free.
But I went into Phyllis Wheatley High School Band
with an 80-piece brass band and I'm the only fiddle player in there.
And I couldn't hear myself play.
You listen to what I say.
Yeah, I know what you're saying.

But I'm happy to be there. I'm SAWING and SAWING and so finally the instructor says, he says, "Son, wouldn't you like to have a horn?" I said, "I sure would." He said, "Okay, we got one left." It was a C melody saxophone. Now, what did I know between a C melody anything, Stanley. But I had to get it and I was ready to take it then. He said, "No, I got to get a confirmation from your parents that somebody will be responsible for it." I'm just a kid.

This time I must have been about 12 or 13 years old, because I started playing professionally at 14. That's how fast it was. He said, "No, you can't take it out today. Bring me a note from your mother or your parents, anybody, tomorrow." And I brought it from my mother. I said, "I know she'll stand for it." And she did. And they let me take it out. C melody. I was so happy with it. I played My Country Tis of Thee." I knew the notes from piano, violin, so all I had to do was learn the fingering of the horn.
I played this thing for a while and just as happy. I marched up Armistice Day down Main Street playing my horn with the lyre and the music, all that, and what have you and enjoyed myself. Happy.
